Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:10:1.hebrew: דנין דיני נפשות - במועד, אבל לא ביום טוב, שאסור משום שבות. ודייקינן מינה: מדדנין במועד, מכלל דאי לא ציית נמי משמתינן ליה במועד:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:10:1.english: The court judges capital cases - on the intermediate days of the Festival, but not on a Festival day [itself], when it is forbidden because of [the rabbinic prohibition of] shevut. And we infer from this: Since [the court] judges during the intermediate days, it follows that if one does not obey, we also ostracize him during the intermediate days:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:11:1.hebrew: אתי רגל ודחי ליה - שאינו נוהג נדוי ברגל:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:11:1.english: The Festival comes and overrides it - [meaning] that the ostracism is not observed during the Festival:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:12:1.hebrew: דלמא לעיוני - הא דתני "דדנין", לא אמרי' דלימא איש פלוני חייב, איש פלוני זכאי, ואיכא למידק מינה דאי לא ציית משמתינן ליה, אלא מעייני בדין, ולא אמרי ליה כלום:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:12:1.english: Perhaps to deliberate - This [statement] that [the baraita] taught, "that they judge," we do not say [that it means] that they say, "So-and-so is liable; so-and-so is innocent," such that one could infer from it that if he does not comply, we ostracize him. Rather, they [only] deliberate over the law, and do not say anything to him:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:14:1.hebrew: מענה את דינו - דכי לא אמרו ליה דינו לאלתר, דעייני ביה, הוה ליה עינוי הדין:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:14:1.english: One who afflicts [i.e., delays] his judgment - For if they do not tell him his verdict immediately, [but rather] they [only] deliberate on it, it constitutes a delay of judgment [literally, an affliction of the judgment]:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:15:1.hebrew: אלא - לעולם דנין דינו וגומרין ממש במועד, ואיכא למידק מינה אי לא ציית משמתינן ליה, ואיכא למשמע מינה דנוהג נמי ברגל. ודאמרת א"כ מימנע משמחת י"ט, הכא במאי עסקינן דאתו מצפרא כו':
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:15:1.english: Rather - Indeed, they judge his case and actually complete it on the Festival. One can infer from this that if he does not obey, we excommunicate him, and one can learn from this that [excommunication] is also practiced on a Festival. And as to what you said, that if so, [the judges] would be prevented from the joy of the Festival, [the Gemara answers:] Here, with what are we dealing? [With a case where the judges] come in the morning, etc.:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:16:1.hebrew: ת"ש מנודה שהתירו לו חכמים - קא סלקא דעתך דהכי קאמר: התירו חכמים לכל מנודה את נידויו ברגל, דאין נידוי נוהג ברגל:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:16:1.english: Come and hear: One who is ostracized, whom the Sages permitted - It enters one's mind [to think] that [the baraita] means: The Sages permitted every ostracized person [to be released from] his ostracism during the Festival, since ostracism does not apply during the Festival:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:17:1.hebrew: דאזיל ופייסיה לבעל דיניה - ברגל, ואתא קמי רבנן והתירו לו חכמים, דהיינו ב"ד שבאותו דור:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:17:1.english: That he went and appeased his litigant - during the Festival, [and he came before the Sages] and the Sages permitted him, [namely] the court of that generation:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:18:1.hebrew: שינהיג צרעתו - שלא יבא אל תוך המחנה, ולא יגלח:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:18:1.english: That he observe his leprosy [practices] - [meaning,] that he not enter into the camp, and not cut his hair:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:18:2.hebrew: הא בימי טומאתו נוהג - מצורע מנהיג צרעתו ברגל:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:18:2.english: This [implies that] during the days of his impurity, he observes - [the leper observes the practices of] his leprosy during the Festival:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:1:1.hebrew: ואי אמרת בקטן אית ליה פלוגתא - חילוק, דקטן דנולד קודם הרגל אינו מגלח ברגל, ואית לן למימר: הואיל ואסור לגלח ברגל, אסור לגלח נמי בימי אבלו. א"כ נמצאת אתה אומר אבילות אפילו בקטן:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:1:1.english: And if you say that a minor has a dispute - [i.e.,] a distinction: [that] one [a minor] who was born before the Festival may not cut his hair on the Festival, and we would have to say: Since it is prohibited to cut hair on the Festival, it is also prohibited to cut it during his days of mourning. If so, you find yourself saying [that the laws of] mourning apply even to a minor:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:20:1.hebrew: לרבות כ"ג - כהן גדול, שנוהג בו צרעת:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:20:1.english: To include a High Priest - that the [laws of] leprosy apply to him:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:20:2.hebrew: הא כהן גדול כל השנה לדידיה כרגל לכולי עלמא דמי - דתנן: כ"ג מקריב אונן, מדאמר לו אהרן למשה "ואכלתי חטאת היום" (ויקרא י׳:י״ט) ולא אמר למשה "והקרבתי", מכלל דהקרבה באנינות מותרת, ולמדנו דכ"ג מקריב אונן. אבל כולי עלמא בשאר ימות השנה, אונן אינו משלח קרבנותיו, כדאמרינן לקמן (מועד קטן דף טו:): שלמים בזמן שהוא שלם, ולא בזמן שהוא אונן. וברגל משלח. וכהן גדול אונן מקריב כל השנה, אלמא כל השנה לדידיה כרגל דמי. וקתני דנוהג בו צרעת, תיפשוט דכל מצורע נוהג צרעתו ברגל:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:20:2.english: But the High Priest, all year round, is for him like a Festival for everyone - as we learned [in a mishna] that the High Priest sacrifices [offerings] while an acute mourner, since Aaron said to Moses, "And [if] I had eaten the sin-offering today" (Leviticus 10:19), and did not say to Moses, "[If] I had sacrificed," [which implies] that sacrificing while in acute mourning [is permitted]. And we learned from this that the High Priest sacrifices while an acute mourner. But everyone else, during the rest of the days of the year, an acute mourner does not send his offerings, as we say below (Moed Katan 15b): Peace-offerings [may be sent] when one is whole, but not when one is an acute mourner; whereas on a Festival he does send. But the High Priest, as an acute mourner, sacrifices all year round. Thus, all year round, for him it is like a Festival. And it teaches that leprosy practices apply to him [the High Priest]. Derive from this that every leper practices [the customs of] his leprosy on a Festival:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:21:1.hebrew: אל תפרעו - גידול שער. והאי קרא גבי מיתת נדב ואביהוא כתיב, ומדאצטריך קרא למישרי להו, מכלל דאחריני אסורין:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:21:1.english: Do not let go loose - [This means] growing out the hair. And this verse is written regarding the death of Nadav and Avihu, and since the verse was needed to permit [this] to them, it follows that others are prohibited:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:2:1.english: One rends for a minor - his garments:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:2:2.hebrew: מפני עגמת נפש - שיבכו הרואין, וירבו בכבוד המת, ולא מפני שהוא אבל:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:2:2.english: Due to grief - so that those who see [him] will weep and will increase [their] honor of the deceased, and not because [the minor] is a mourner:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:3:1.hebrew: מי קתני הא אסורין - דמשמע מהברייתא האסורין לגלח במועד, אסורין לגלח באבל:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:3:1.english: Is it taught: 'these are prohibited' - For [the baraita] implies that those who are prohibited from having a haircut during the Festival are [also] prohibited from having a haircut during mourning:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:3:2.hebrew: יש מהן אסורין - בשאר כל אדם, שאסורין לגלח במועד, הם אסורין לגלח בימי אבלן:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:3:2.english: There are among them [some who are] prohibited - With regard to all other people who are prohibited from taking a haircut during the Festival, they are [also] prohibited from taking a haircut during the days of their mourning:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:3:3.hebrew: ויש מהן מותרין - כגון קטן זה שנולד קודם הרגל, שאסור לגלח ברגל, מותר לגלח בימי אבלו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:3:3.english: And there are among them those who are permitted - For example, this baby who was born before the Festival: although it is prohibited to have a haircut during the Festival, [the baby] is permitted to have a haircut during the days of his mourning:

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:9:1.english: The positive mitzva of the community comes - [as it is written]: "And you shall rejoice":

Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:9:2.hebrew: ודחי עשה דיחיד - והעשה דיחיד היא אבל, דכתיב (ירמיהו ו׳:כ״ו): "אבל יחיד עשי לך":
Rashi on Moed Katan 14b:9:2.english: And it overrides the positive mitzva of the individual - [The positive mitzva of the individual is] mourning, as it is written (Jeremiah 6:26): "Make for yourself mourning as for an only son":

Tosafot on Moed Katan 14b:10:1.hebrew: מהו שינהוג נידויו ברגל - והקשה הרב: הא ליכא אלא עשה, ואין עשה דוחה עשה! ואפילו עשה ליכא, אלא עזרא גזר, כדלקמן (מועד קטן דף טז.). והא לאו קושיא היא, דהא נידוי דחי לאו דמקלל חברו, דאיכא לאו, ושמא מסוטה ילפינן. ועוד, כיון שעבר על דברי הדיינין, הרי יש כאן עשה דרבים:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 14b:10:1.english: What is the halakha [as to whether] his ostracism should be observed on the Festival - And the Rav [i.e., a prior authority] raised a difficulty: There is only a positive commandment [of rejoicing on the Festival here], and a positive commandment does not override a positive commandment! And there is not even a positive commandment, but rather Ezra decreed [it], as [stated] below (Moed Katan 16a). But this is not a difficulty, for ostracism overrides the prohibition against cursing one's fellow, even though there is a prohibition there [in cursing]; and perhaps we derive [this] from the sotah. [That is, one might counter that the source for such overriding is the sotah, so the case is not a proof.] Furthermore, since he transgressed the words of the judges, there is here a positive commandment of the public:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 14b:10:2.hebrew: ואי לא ציית דינא משמתינן ליה - תימה: לימא דאי לא צית דינא נחתינן לנכסיה? מיהו פריך שפיר:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 14b:10:2.english: "And if he does not heed the judgment, we ostracize him" - It is astonishing: Let [the baraita] say that if he does not heed the judgment, we go down to his property [to seize it]! However, [the Gemara] does ask well [from this baraita]:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 14b:13:1.hebrew: ממנעי משמחת י"ט - הקשה בתוס' הר"א: היכי קשה ליה? דהא ממנעי משמחת י"ט מאכילה ושתיה, וגוף ההריגה דהוא מלאכה לא חיישינן! ונראה לי: מדאסר רחמנא הבערת בת כהן בשבת, מכלל דבמועד שרי; אי נמי כיון שהיא מצוה לצורך י"ט, קרינא בה:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 14b:13:1.english: They are prevented from the rejoicing of the Festival - It is asked in the Tosafot of Rabbi Eliezer: Why is this difficult for him? For they are prevented from the rejoicing of the Festival [only] through eating and drinking, but the act of the execution itself, which is labor, we do not [consider as] a concern! And it seems to me: since the Merciful One forbade the burning of a priest's daughter on Shabbat, it follows that on a Festival it is permitted; alternatively, since it is a commandment [performed] for the need of the Festival, we read it [as applying] to it:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 14b:14:1.hebrew: נמצאת אתה מענה את דינו - קשיא לן: דבפ' אחד דיני ממונות (סנהדרין דף לה.) בשמעתין דלפיכך אין דנין (. בשבת), מוכח דעינוי הדין לא שייך עד שילינוהו אחר שיגמור הדין. וכי תימא דלעיוני דהכא היינו גמר דין, ולא יהרגוהו עדיין עד אחר הרגל, א"כ אמאי פריך? לימא לעיוני בעלמא בלא גמר דין, ולא יעשוהו גמר דין עד אחר המועד! וי"ל דמשתכחי, אף על גב דאיכא סופרי דיינין הכותבים דברי כל אחד, מ"מ הסברא אשר בלב משתכח. ומהאי טעמא אמרינן (שם) דאין דנין בערב שבת, דליבא דאינשי אינשי:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 14b:14:1.english: You find that you are perverting his judgment - It is difficult for us: for in the chapter [entitled] Echad Dinei Mamonot (Sanhedrin 35a), in the passage [that says] "therefore they do not judge [on Shabbat]," it is proven that the perversion of justice does not apply until they leave him [undecided] overnight after the judgment is completed. And if you say that the "deliberating" here means the conclusion of the judgment, and they would not yet execute him until after the Festival — if so, why does [Rav Yosef] challenge? Let [Rav Huna] say [that it means] mere deliberating, without concluding the judgment, and they would not make it a concluded judgment until after the Festival! And one can answer that [the reasoning] is forgotten: even though there are court scribes who write the words of each one, nevertheless the reasoning that is in the heart is forgotten. And for this reason we say (there) that they do not judge on the eve of Shabbat, for people's hearts [forget] — they forget:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 14b:16:1.hebrew: אמר אביי ת"ש מנודה שהתירו כו' - אביי לטעמיה, דדחי "ודלמא לעיוני", ואין חושב ראייה להוכחה דלעיל. ואע"ג דדחי, דאי לא תימא, דקאמ' לא חש באותו דיחוי, ואפי' נראה דיחוי, ה"נ מסתברא; מ"מ נוכל לומר "לעיוני", בלאו הכי נמי מסתברא:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 14b:16:1.english: Abaye said: Come and hear: [A case of] one who is ostracized, that [the Sages] permitted, etc. - Abaye is consistent with his reasoning, for he rejected [the earlier proof] with "perhaps it was for looking over [the hair]", and he does not consider it a proof for the demonstration above. And although he rejected [it] — for if you do not say so, [then] that which [the Gemara] says, he did not pay heed to that rejection, and even if a rejection is apparent, this too is reasonable; nevertheless, we can say "for looking over [the hair]"; even without this, it is also reasonable:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 14b:20:1.hebrew: והא כ"ג דכל השנה כולה כרגל כו' - משמע דאם אין מנודה נוהג נידוי ברגל, הוא הדין כ"ג אינו נוהג נידוי כלל. וקשה, דהא כ"ג דן ודנין אותו, ואי לא ציית דינא (לא) משמתינן ליה! ולמאי דפרישית לעיל, דנוכל לומר למיחת לנכסיה, ניחא:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 14b:20:1.english: "And the High Priest, for the entire year is like a Festival," etc. - This implies that if a person under a ban does not observe the ban on a Festival, the same applies to the High Priest: he does not observe a ban at all. And this is difficult, for the High Priest judges and is judged, and if he does not obey the law, do we not place him under a ban? But according to what I explained above, that we can say [that the court] may descend to his property, it is well:

Tosafot on Moed Katan 14b:9:1.hebrew: עשה דיחיד - משמע דאבילות איכא עשה דאורייתא, מדלא קאמר "ודחי עשה דרבנן". והאי דקאמר לעיל (מועד קטן דף יא:): לא מבעיא ימי אבלו דרבנן, היינו עשיית מלאכה, דנפקא לן (לקמן מועד קטן טו:) באסמכתא מ"והפכתי חגיכם לאבל"; אבל גוף האבילות דאורייתא. מיהו נראה לי דשמחת הרגל נמי דרבנן, ו"שמחת" היינו בשלמי שמחה, כדאיתא בחגיגה (ח.):
Tosafot on Moed Katan 14b:9:1.english: The positive mitzva of the individual - This implies that mourning involves a positive mitzva from the Torah, since [the Gemara] did not say "and it overrides a rabbinic positive mitzva." And as for that which [the Gemara] says above (Moed Katan 11b): "It is not necessary [to say] that the days of his mourning are rabbinic," that refers to performing labor, which we derive (below, Moed Katan 15b) as an asmakhta from [the verse] "And I will turn your festivals into mourning"; but the essence of mourning is from the Torah. Nevertheless, it seems to me that the rejoicing of the Festival is also rabbinic, and "you shall rejoice" refers to the peace-offerings of rejoicing, as stated in Chagigah (8a):
